# m.forex.previous_day_bar

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

The previous UTC day's open, high, low, close, and volume of each currency pair.

Call it from a session `m`, made with `dm.MassiveSession()`:

```python
m.forex.previous_day_bar(symbols, *, on_error=None)
```

- [Methods](README.md#query-methods): `fetch()`, `poll(interval)`
- Read from: REST
- `poll()` by default: `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`, which holds only the latest poll's rows, one row per `Symbol`
- `poll(interval, mode=dm.PollMode.APPEND)`: appends each new state of a row, identified by `Symbol` and `TimestampStart`

[Dataset index](README.md)

## Arguments

A linked argument follows its rule under [shared arguments](README.md#shared-arguments) on the dataset index.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`symbols`](README.md#symbols) | Currency pairs, such as `C:EURUSD`. `dm.ALL` is refused; for every pair's bar of one day, use `m.forex.bars(dm.ALL, dm.Timespan.DAY).history(day, day)`. |
| [`on_error`](README.md#on_error) | What a bad symbol or row does in this call (`dm.ErrorPolicy`). None, the default, takes each cause from the session's `MassiveConfig.on_error`. |

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The row's instrument, as Massive's ticker. From REST `T`: "The exchange symbol that this item is traded under." |
| `Date` | String | The trading day of the bar, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: the UTC date of `TimestampStart` for an intraday or 1-day bar, and null for a bar that spans more than one date (several days, a week or longer, or an intraday bar that crosses midnight). Joining an intraday row to the same day's daily bar on `Date` attaches values not known until that day ended, and a null `Date` matches another null, so join longer bars on `TimestampEnd`. |
| `TimestampStart` | Instant | The start of the bar's window, as an Instant. A bar of a day or longer starts at 00:00 UTC of its window's first day (a week's Sunday, a month's, quarter's, or year's 1st), whichever source serves it. A bar of a day or longer stamped at a time or on a day Massive is not known to use is withheld, with a WARNING, since which day it covers is not known. Every other stamp, as each source sends it (quoted next), is moved there. From REST `t`: "The Unix millisecond timestamp for the start of the aggregate window." |
| `TimestampEnd` | Instant | The exclusive end of the bar's window, as an Instant: the first instant at which the bar is complete, so an as-of join on it, `t.aj(bars, on=["Symbol", "Timestamp>=TimestampEnd"])`, never attaches a bar that is still open. It is when the window closes, not when Massive published the bar, and Massive may correct a bar later. An intraday bar ends at Massive's `e` where the WebSocket sends one, else its length after its start; a WARNING says when the two differ. A bar of a day or longer ends at 00:00 UTC after its window's last day. A row read before its window ended has `TimestampInsert` before `TimestampEnd`, and its values can still change; `t.where("TimestampEnd <= TimestampInsert")` keeps only the rows read after their window ended. That test reads the local clock, which can be off, and a row read within moments of its end, or from a delayed feed, may still lack the window's last trades; an end set later than the window's (an index day's extra hour, a stamp kept as sent) only keeps a finished row out longer. |
| `Open` | double | The open price for the symbol in the given time period. |
| `High` | double | The highest price for the symbol in the given time period. |
| `Low` | double | The lowest price for the symbol in the given time period. |
| `Close` | double | The close price for the symbol in the given time period. |
| `Volume` | double | The trading volume of the symbol in the given time period. |
| `Vwap` | double | The volume weighted average price. |
| `Transactions` | long | The number of transactions in the aggregate window. |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, by the local clock. Rows that arrive together share it. It isn't Massive's time, and later rows can carry earlier times. In a `poll()` table, it's the time of the poll the row's values came from. |
